title: "Getting started"

## Installing

phpolars runs on PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5, non-thread-safe (NTS) builds, on Linux and macOS. Install it with [PIE](https://github.com/php/pie), PHP's extension installer:

```sh
pie install phpstats/phpolars
```

On Linux on x86_64 and arm64 with glibc 2.34 or later, PIE downloads a prebuilt binary. On other platforms, including macOS, it builds the extension from source, which needs a stable Rust toolchain and libclang and takes several minutes. PIE then enables the extension in php.ini. Under PHP-FPM, restart FPM afterwards so that its workers load the extension. [Deployment](deployment.qmd) covers servers, Laravel Forge, Laravel Herd, and manual installs.

## Checking the installation

```sh
php -r 'echo phpversion("php_polars"), PHP_EOL;'
```

The command prints the installed version, such as `0.2.2`. It checks the CLI. PHP-FPM reads its own php.ini, so check a web request separately, for example with `extension_loaded('php_polars')` in a page.

## A starter script

phpolars needs no Composer packages. Download the example data, `penguins.csv`: body measurements of 344 penguins near Palmer Station, Antarctica, from the R `palmerpenguins` package ([penguins](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#penguins)). Missing values are written `NA`.

```sh
mkdir phpolars-start && cd phpolars-start
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/datasets/main/csv/penguins.csv
```

Runnable script: [starter.php](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/phpolars/main/docs/examples/starter.php).

{{< include examples/_starter.md >}}

## Imports

Classes such as `Phpolars\DataFrame` live in the `Phpolars` namespace, and so do the functions, which need `use function`. The examples on this page use these:

```php
use function Phpolars\{col, len, lit, read_csv, scan_csv, when};
```

The examples below read the same `penguins.csv`, with `nullValues: 'NA'` so that `NA` entries become nulls.

## A first query

{{< include examples/_select.md >}}

Strings passed where py-polars expects an expression input, such as `select()`, name columns. Use `lit()` for a string value there. In comparisons and arithmetic, strings are literals: `col('island')->ne('Torgersen')`. A `when()` chain without `otherwise()` gives null where no condition holds, as for the penguin without a body mass.

## Grouping

{{< include examples/_group-by.md >}}

`groupBy()` follows py-polars and does not keep group order unless `maintainOrder: true` is passed.

## Lazy queries

A `DataFrame` runs each method immediately. A `LazyFrame` records operations and runs them when `collect()` is called. `scan_csv()` creates a lazy query. Polars optimizes the column selection and the filters before running it, so the reader converts only the columns that the query uses and drops filtered rows as it parses them. The reader still reads the whole file. [Query a large CSV file lazily](examples/lazy-csv.qmd) walks through a query plan.

{{< include examples/_lazy.md >}}

## Missing values

phpolars follows Polars: a missing value is `null`, aggregates such as `sum()` and `mean()` skip it, and `null` sorts first. phibble and phplyr follow R and dplyr instead. [phibble and phplyr](phibble.qmd#missing-values) compares the two.
